proposals.before: His father, Chang Jing, served as prefect of Suining in Sichuan.
proposals.after: His father, Chang Jing, served as prefect of Suiding in Sichuan.
proposals.reason: 綏定府 is Suiding Prefecture; “Suining” misidentifies the place.

proposals.before: His father Chang Jing was prefect of Suining Prefecture in Sichuan.
proposals.after: His father Chang Jing was prefect of Suiding Prefecture in Sichuan.
proposals.reason: 綏定府 is Suiding Prefecture; “Suining” misidentifies the place.

proposals.before: Zongshi Zaimu, styled Jingxiu, was enrolled in the Manchu Bordered Blue Banner and a fifth-generation descendant of Prince Xunqin Yunli.
proposals.after: Zongshi Zaimu, styled Jingxiu, was enrolled in the Manchu Bordered Blue Banner and a fifth-generation descendant of Prince Xunqin Yunti.
proposals.reason: The source names 允禵 (Yunti), not Yunli; these are different imperial princes.

proposals.before: Zongshi Zaimu, styled Jingxiu, was enrolled in the Manchu Bordered Blue Banner and was fifth-generation descendant of Prince Xunqin Yunli.
proposals.after: Zongshi Zaimu, styled Jingxiu, was enrolled in the Manchu Bordered Blue Banner and was a fifth-generation descendant of Prince Xunqin Yunti.
proposals.reason: The source names 允禵 (Yunti), not Yunli; the repair also supplies the missing article.

proposals.before: His family found letters to his brother Heng Guang and son Yu saying, "Our family has enjoyed the dynasty's favor for generations and ought to repay it with all our strength.
proposals.after: His family found letters to his brother Heng Guang and son Yuwen saying, "Our family has enjoyed the dynasty's favor for generations and ought to repay it with all our strength.
proposals.reason: The source gives the son’s full name 裕文, Yuwen; “Yu” truncates it.

proposals.before: His family found his letter to his younger brother Heng Guang and son Yu, saying, "Our family has received the state's grace for generations and ought to repay it with all our strength.
proposals.after: His family found his letter to his younger brother Heng Guang and son Yuwen, saying, "Our family has received the state's grace for generations and ought to repay it with all our strength.
proposals.reason: The source gives the son’s full name 裕文, Yuwen; “Yu” truncates it.

proposals.before: The court posthumously made him junior guardian of the heir apparent, granted a hereditary second-class commandery chariot captaincy, and gave him the posthumous name Zhongsu, "Loyal and Stern."
proposals.after: The court posthumously made him Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, granted a hereditary second-class commandery chariot captaincy, and gave him the posthumous name Zhongsu, "Loyal and Stern."
proposals.reason: 太子太保 is Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, not the junior-guardian office 太子少保.

proposals.before: When the matter was reported he was posthumously made Junior Guardian of the Heir Apparent, granted a hereditary second-class commandery chariot captaincy, and given the posthumous name Zhongsu.
proposals.after: When the matter was reported he was posthumously made Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, granted a hereditary second-class commandery chariot captaincy, and given the posthumous name Zhongsu.
proposals.reason: 太子太保 is Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, not the junior-guardian office 太子少保.

proposals.before: His family bore his coffin home for burial, and mourners set out offerings along the route for hundreds of miles.
proposals.after: His family bore his coffin home for burial, and mourners set out offerings along the route for several hundred li.
proposals.reason: Chinese 數百里 means several hundred li, not statute miles; the idiomatic rendering invents a Western distance unit.

proposals.before: When Shizheng went to fight in Taiwan and the battle went badly, he once carried Rangli on his back to safety, and the whole army admired the deed.
proposals.after: When Shizheng went to aid Taiwan and the battle went badly, he once carried Rangli on his back to safety, and the whole army admired the deed.
proposals.reason: Chinese 援 means to aid/reinforce, not merely to fight; the literal already has "aid".

proposals.before: Men such as Zhi Rui held little power and stood alone, struggling to shore up the situation and hoping to save the dynasty from a single corner of the empire;
proposals.after: Men such as Zhi Jun held little power and stood alone, struggling to shore up the situation and hoping to save the dynasty from a single corner of the empire;
proposals.reason: Chinese names 志鈞 (Zhi Jun); English wrongly substitutes Zhi Rui (志銳), the chapter subject.

proposals.before: Zhi Rui and others had light authority and stood alone, propping up the situation with difficulty, thinking to save the whole realm from one corner;
proposals.after: Zhi Jun and others had light authority and stood alone, propping up the situation with difficulty, thinking to save the whole realm from one corner;
proposals.reason: Chinese 志鈞 must be rendered Zhi Jun, not Zhi Rui.

decisions.reason: s0005 names 四川綏定府; Suining (遂寧) is a different place, so Suiding correctly restores the prefecture.
The literal likewise misreads 綏定府 as Suining Prefecture; Suiding Prefecture matches the Chinese place-name.
s0055 names 恂勤郡王允禵; Yunli would be a different prince (允禮), so Yunti is the required correction.
The literal repeats Yunli for 允禵; Yunti is correct, and adding the article before fifth-generation is grammatical without changing sense.
s0153 gives the son as 裕文; truncating to Yu drops 文 and invents a shorter name.
The literal also shortens 裕文 to Yu; Yuwen restores the full personal name from the source.
s0171 awards 太子太保 (Grand Guardian), not 太子少保 (Junior Guardian); the proposed title is accurate.
The literal mislabels 太子太保 as Junior Guardian; Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent is the standard rendering of 太保.
數百里 is several hundred li; rendering it as hundreds of miles substitutes a different unit and overstates the distance.
詩正援台灣 uses 援 ‘aid/reinforce’; ‘went to fight in Taiwan’ drops that sense, while ‘went to aid Taiwan’ matches the verb.
s0280 opens with 志鈞等, a different person from chapter subject 志銳; Zhi Jun is required.
The literal likewise substitutes Zhi Rui for 志鈞; Zhi Jun restores the named figure in the historian’s comment.
